entities.title: The rules the README promises
entities.summary: Waves of stone, crystal and iron rocks, drones, pods, blink, streaks and lives, with the README's numbers.
entities.statement: Large rocks split into two medium and medium into two small; crystal splits in three, is worth double and may drop a pod; iron takes two hits, is worth triple and appears from wave 3. Drones cross and shoot; the hunter aims, from wave 3. Blink jumps 230 px with half a second's guard and recharges in 3 s. Hits within 1.6 s build a streak; every 5 raise the multiplier, up to ×4. Three ships each, another every 10,000 points; ships that touch are both lost.
entities.rationale: These rules, and their numbers, are what the README tells players.
acceptanceCriteria: Stone scores 25, 60 and 120 for large, medium and small; crystal double; iron triple.
The large drone is worth 250, the hunter 700, a versus takedown 500, each multiplied by the streak.
The game ends when every player is out of ships.

entities.title: Scores can't be faked
entities.summary: A score on the table is only ever what the server's replay of the game computed.
entities.statement: The server issues each game's seed, replays the recorded controls of every player with the same engine before listing any score, and accepts each seed once.
entities.rationale: A public table is only worth climbing if nobody can type a score into it.
acceptanceCriteria: A recording that does not play exactly one whole game is refused.
A recording made with another seed does not replay to the same scores.

entities.title: Friends fly on their own devices
entities.summary: Up to nine pilots play one game online, each on their own computer, phone or tablet, in co-op or versus.
entities.statement: An online game started from the multiplayer page is played by two to nine signed-in pilots on as many devices, who all see exactly the same game. Each browser flies one pilot; there is no game for several pilots on one device.

origin.description: Shatterbelt's README, Controls and Playing online.

entities.title: Online games go on the table
entities.summary: An online game is entered on the public table like any other, each pilot under their own name.
entities.statement: At the end of an online game each pilot who made the table names themselves on their own screen, and the host's browser sends the game with every name.

entities.title: Playing needs a sign-in
entities.summary: The game and its score API are for players signed in to icelander.net; the table stays public.
entities.statement: The game's page, a new game's seed and a score submission need a sign-in to icelander.net with the games:play role. The table, as JSON or as a page, needs none.

origin.description: The repository README: every game needs icelander.net's sign-in; the high-score tables stay public.

entities.title: Keyboard, gamepad or touch
entities.summary: Every pilot can fly with the keyboard, a gamepad or the touch buttons.
entities.statement: Arrows or WASD (and the numpad) turn, thrust and blink, Space or Enter fires; a gamepad's stick, d-pad and buttons do the same; phones and tablets get on-screen buttons.

entities.title: Only a name is stored
entities.summary: A score is stored with a name of up to 12 characters, and nothing else about the player.
entities.statement: The table stores a name of up to 12 plain characters with each score, and the game's wave, mode and number of players. No email address or other personal data is stored.

entities.title: The game plays without the server
entities.summary: When the score server can't be reached, the game still plays and its scores stay on the device.
entities.statement: A game whose seed the server could not issue still plays; its scores can go only on the device's own top ten, which is kept in the browser either way.

entities.title: An original game
entities.summary: Shatterbelt belongs to the rock-shooter genre but copies no game in it.
entities.statement: Shatterbelt's name, look, sounds, rules for crystal and iron rocks, pods, blink, streaks, drones and multiplayer are its own.
